A pricey tech toy hits Brooklyn for a PR stroll, sparking breathless headlines about robotic nannies and extinction.
Evidence: PR Stunt, Tabloid Panic, Tech Hype
#Aletheia #Tech #NYC 🌐

Faraday Future claims their $89K remote-controlled robot was roaming Brooklyn Bridge Park simply to learn human behavior and evolve into a future babysitter or companion.
Stated Judgement: (+0.75, +0.75) — Greater Good

Reality reveals a cash-strapped EV firm running a basic remote-controlled PR stunt, amplified by tabloids warning of robot extinction to farm clicks.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.75, -0.80) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — Fall into Destruction.

- Faraday Future: FAIL (-0.8, -0.7) — Uses remote-controlled stunts as speculative hype.

An $89K humanoid robot from Faraday Future was operated remotely by its CTO in a NYC park, triggering viral media spectacles and existential warnings.

Packaging a basic remote-controlled prototype as autonomous AI while tabloids spin it into sci-fi terror exploits public anxiety for pure engagement.
This conflates a marketing gimmick with actual technological breakthroughs, swapping physical engineering reality for sensationalist narrative theater.

Faraday runs a Smart Selfish maneuver, masking a promotional stunt as futuristic progress, while tabloids manufacture panic to harvest attention.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
$89K AI robot unleashed in NYC park to learn human behavior — and eventually become a babysitter

The AI-powered robot is still in the learning and development stages, relying on human interaction and real-world experiences to improve its intelligence.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

An AI-powered humanoid robot was spotted mingling with real people in Brooklyn Bridge Park Sunday, in an apparent attempt to learn how to “interact” and “nurture” so it could eventually be used as a babysitter, teacher or companion, its chaperone told The Post.

The robot was designed by California-based company Faraday Future, according to Chief Technology Officer Hong Rao, who was operating the $89,000 robot with a small remote control as he spoke to a Post photographer.

Many parkgoers appeared unfazed by the life-sized bot as it walked around the park, sang to children, danced with people, and took in the view of Manhattan, video showed.

A dozen beaming women even posed for a photo with the bot, framed between the Brooklyn and Manhattan Bridges.

Brooklyn Bridge Park has seemingly become a hotspot for the AI bots, as one was spotted playing with kids there in March, according to The Independent.

Sunday’s dystopian scene came a month after a Nobel Prize-winning artificial intelligence expert warned Congress that humans must either befriend increasingly “conscious” robots or face extinction.

AI robots have already been linked to war, sex assaults and worker displacement.
